conversation.confirmation_assistant_template: Order line {order_line_id} is now locked for return processing. Please provide the return reason, quantity, number of packages, preferred shipping method, and any optional notes.
conversation.continue_match_template: Great! Using {anchor_type} '{anchor_value}', I found {count} matching candidate order(s). Please review the updated list and confirm the item being returned.
conversation.continue_no_match_template: I checked for {anchor_type} '{anchor_value}', but still couldn't locate a matching order in our systems. Please double-check the number or try searching by customer phone, email, or exact SKU.
conversation.greeting_response: Hi there! I'm your AI Copilot, ready to help you with this return. What details do you have? You can give me an order number, a customer's name and zip code, or even just tell me what's wrong with the item.
conversation.initial_match_template: I located {count} matching order(s) for {anchor_type} '{anchor_value}'. Please review the evidence below and confirm the exact customer and order line to proceed.
conversation.initial_no_match_template: I searched our order records for {anchor_type} '{anchor_value}', but couldn't find a direct match. Could you provide another identifier such as an order number, customer ID, tracking number, or SKU?
conversation.submission_assistant_template: Return session {session_id} has been created and transferred to Return Support processing.

identification_fields.description: The colour of the item. Configured and enabled; whether it can be searched depends on the active knowledge-graph schema carrying a colour property. It does not today, so this signal is reported back to the associate as one that could not be used rather than silently dropped -- and matching a colour word against product_description instead would put "Blue Ridge Faucet" in front of someone who said the tap was blue. The day a colour property is projected, one `searches` entry here turns it on.
